What is the difference between Route 53 DNS query logging and Resolver Query Logging?

Route 53 DNS query logging records the public queries received for public hosted zones and only writes to CloudWatch Logs. Resolver Query Logging records all DNS queries from the resources in the VPC, from on-prem via inbound endpoints, from outbound endpoints, and from DNS Firewall, to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose, with possible sharing via AWS RAM.

Penetration testing & DDoS simulation on AWS
Before defending yourself, you must know what you are allowed to test on your own AWS account without having your account suspended.
The problem: testing without harming others

A **pentest** simulates an attacker before the real one shows up. But your EC2 instance runs on **shared** hardware: a test that is too massive can disturb AWS or third parties. Hence a policy: 8 services can be tested **without approval**, and certain actions are **forbidden**.
The 8 services testable without approval
EC2, NAT Gateways, ELB
Port scanning, OS and application testing: the classic case.
RDS and Aurora
Exposed database configuration, weak passwords.
CloudFront
CDN distribution at the edge.
Exposed REST/HTTP APIs.
Lambda and Lambda@Edge
Serverless functions and their inputs.
Lightsail and Beanstalk
Simplified servers and application environments.
Allowed vs Forbidden
without approval
Pentest on the 8 listed services
On YOUR resources, in YOUR account
Scan, vulnerability testing, authentication testing
You keep a record (logs, dates, scope)
Regular security audit of an application that you own.
Forbidden
DNS zone walking via Route 53 hosted zones
DoS / DDoS, including simulated ones
Port flooding, protocol flooding
Request flooding (login flooding, API request flooding)
Never do it without going through the official AWS channel (DDoS simulation via an approved partner).

Classic question: "Can I run a penetration test on my EC2 instance without notifying AWS?" Yes (EC2 is one of the 8 services). "Can I run a DDoS load test on my ELB?" No, forbidden, except for a supervised DDoS simulation with an approved partner.
